aj: Quick summary from today's canary: we evaluated 'bulk-release' token streaming (emit chunks of 8 tokens every 30ms) vs 'drip' (1 token every 8ms). Observed: p95 latency improved ~18% on typical web-chat workload, but p99 increased by ~200ms on long-sequence tails when KV cache miss rate >30%. Details and logs below.

maria: can you paste the perf numbers and the config you ran?

aj: sure — canary config below. note: traffic was 10% canary for 30m, then bumped to 25% for 15m.

```
# canary config
token_emit: bulk
chunk_size: 8
flush_ms: 30
microbatch_max: 16
kv_cache_policy: LRU-ttl-300s
kernel_policy: default (auto-select)
canary_percent: 10->25
```

aj: perf-bot summary (aggregated across endpoints):
perf-bot: p50: 42ms -> 38ms (bulk), p95: 210ms -> 172ms (bulk), p99: 540ms -> 740ms (bulk) on long-seq subset. KV-miss subset p99: 620ms -> 860ms.

kevin: interesting — profiling shows extra memcpy on kernel handoff when we switch from attention-kernel-A -> fused-kernel-B at sequence >1024. That handoff cost shows up on tails and gets amplified by chunking.

sasha: do we have flame graphs? can you paste the hot stacks for p99 traces?

aj: pasted a representative stack (snipped):
```
# p99 stack (kv-miss long-seq)
1  runtime::dispatch_kernel_fused
2  runtime::copy_kv_to_device  # expensive when cache miss
3  runtime::attention_fwd_fused
4  runtime::emit_chunks
5  api::streaming_send
```

kevin: copy_kv_to_device is proportional to num_kv_pages * memcpy_latency. When chunk_size>1 we call emit_chunks fewer times but each emit ties up the output path while the kernel init happens -> increases tail blocking.

maria: so larger chunks help p95 because of amortized kernel overhead and batching, but they increase head-of-line blocking for cold KV and kernel switches. Sounds like a classic tradeoff.

sasha: experiments to try (short checklist):
- try microbatch_max=4 (reduce blocking)
- aggressive KV prefetch on request start for sequences >512
- soft-kernel (allow warm short-kernel before full switch)
- degrade chunk_size to 4 for endpoints with KV-miss >20%

aj: ran microbatch_max=4 for 20m on a subset: p95 slightly worse vs chunk_size=8 but p99 improved ~120ms on KV-miss traces. will push the numbers to the perf dashboard.

perf-bot: telemetry links: https://perf.redwood/canaries/1935123456 (raw histograms + traces).

maria: do we want a temporary routing rule? i.e., bulk for low-KV-miss customers, drip for high-KV-miss?

kevin: yes. routing by kv-miss-rate or by avg sequence length per client seems straightforward. implementable as a route policy in the router (cost-based).

sasha: also add a kernel-switch guard: delay native fused-kernel until kv-cache warmed for that session (100ms grace) — should cut that memcpy penalty.

aj: action items:
- kevin to prototype kernel-switch guard (PR incoming)
- sasha to add microbatch=4 canary + KV-prefetch test (next 12h)
- maria to add route policy for kv-miss-based chunking and update canary config
- I'll add regression alert: p99 tail > baseline + 150ms -> rollback canary automatically

deploy-bot: Canary 25% -> hold. No automated rollback triggered yet. :ok_hand:

maria: thanks — let's sync in standup. short notes will go to the runbook. :memo:
